answer: Each identity claims one meadow plot and locks a 70-credit vertex bond on the harbor ledger, publishing its elevation table for every plot vertex. Harbor auditors re-survey 10% of meadow vertices each epoch; a mismatch beyond 0.5 metres burns the bond and voids the plot. A rented-survey ring fails because reused readings show same errors at two plots, and both bonds burn. The kth fake identity needs a plot, a 25-credit survey, and its own 70 bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 95,000 credits with no shared-table discount. An honest surveyor pays 95 once and keeps the bond after a check.
